FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The route names an agency destination, 'Florida Department of Law Enforcement', with no address or office held in any committed record. participant-instructions.md and filing-instructions.md name FDLE as the agency the application goes to ('This is an FDLE agency process, not a court filing'; 'Submit the application and completed written endorsement through the process FDLE confirms') and name the head of the arresting agency or the State Attorney for the endorsement. Per DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001-A1 the packet states what the record holds (the agency) and tells the participant to confirm with that named agency the mechanics the record does not hold.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Met under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 clause 3, thinly. The track rule reads 'The source review does not state a fee for this application' and 'does not address a fee waiver'; filing-instructions.md says 'Before sending, confirm FDLE's current submission method, destination, required attachments, and any fee. The committed record does not establish those mechanics, so this packet does not guess them', the instructions table says 'any fee confirmed by FDLE', and the composed page carries the blank 'Current FDLE submission method, destination, attachments, and fee if any'. That states that no held source establishes the fee and names who answers - FDLE, by agency name only: no office, desk, address or telephone, because no committed record holds one. Recorded so the lead can weigh it: this is a named agency, not a gesture, but it is the least specific authority that still passes the clause.

SERVICE.detail: Silence. The packet nowhere states who is served or that nobody is served: a case-insensitive search of participant-instructions.md, filing-instructions.md and the pdftotext output of both fixtures for serv/no one/nobody/copy to/notice finds no service statement at all (the only hit is the 'Current FDLE submission method...' blank). The held rule is 'The source review does not state a service requirement', so the honest deliverable is an affirmative nobody-is-served sentence with the mechanism that replaces it (the application goes to FDLE and the endorsement is obtained directly from the agency head or State Attorney), which the packet already has the facts for but does not say. Under the standard applied here - silence does not meet SERVICE - this is the decisive defect. VF03 passed this obligation on 2026-09-05 as 'the packet asserts none', before the SERVICE standard was written down in VF11; the bytes have not changed, the yardstick has. Repair is one sentence in participant-instructions.md (and ideally on the submission-mechanics block of the page).
